name: Place recruiting's reads on the leads' review and the partners' domain read
text_content:
Type: process

Recruiting carries three standing reads and none of them has a placement yet. The pipeline read is one standing line at the weekly leads' review, carrying per open seat the stage counts, the candidates past window, the source mix, and the seat's age; the team recommends it be read under the load reading, since an open seat is a load on adjacent nodes, and it enters either under one of Session 4's eight agenda items or as a ninth line (P28, I22, S4 P26). Behind it the stack surfaces continuously and without anyone asking: any candidate outside the four states, any candidate past the response window with no dated action, any seat open past three consecutive leads' reviews, sent to the domain lead and the Maitre d. A seat past three reviews goes to the partners' review as a possible node-overload entry. The house response window is five days from any stage's completion to a sent decision, shortenable on a sheet and never lengthenable (P29). The candidate pulse's single open question travels with every decision, hire or decline, and is read monthly at the partners' domain read by the Maitre d, for the process and never for the person, anonymized (P30, I16). The source-dominance and stage-rate read runs at the leads' review with no target and no figure (P26). Readiness rows 42 and 58 check the placements. No candidate's name appears in the leads' review record.

Filed by Session 5 of the Scaling People translation program. Session task 86ajgmhm4. Reasoning lives on the S5 page of the Sŏn Operating System doc 2ky45bmy-17253.
